errorCodes.meaning: The domain does not accept self-registration, or not by the admission kind presented. did-management/server/info says which domains do, and how.
The invite or voucher does not admit this registrant here. `reason` says why.
The domain holds the most self-registered accounts it admits. Space may free up as accounts expire.
The registrant already holds an account on this service. Later publications use did-management/did/register as the account holder.
The log failed verification, or does not establish the DID the slot names (`domain` and `path`).
The document's `issuer` is neither the DID the log establishes nor a `did:scid` alias that DID's current document lists, or the proof's key is not an `authentication` method of that document.
The path breaks the domain's path rules for self-registered accounts, or the invite's path prefix.
The submitted `domain` is not a known hosting domain on this consumer. See [the category conventions](../../../_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md#2-unknown-domain-error).

AccountReferral.description: A Referral as the service recorded it on an account, with whether anything other than the registrant's own word supports it.

verified.description: `true` when the admission evidence supports it: a voucher whose issuer is `via`, or an invite whose administrator set the referral when issuing it. `false`: the registrant's own claim, recorded for attribution only.

AccountReferral.title: AccountReferral

AccountState.description: Where an account stands in the inactivity lifecycle. `active`: its DIDs are served. `warned`: its DIDs are served, `disableAt` is near, and the service has sent at least one expiry notice. `disabled`: its DIDs are not served; the holder may still renew until `purgeAt`. A purged account no longer exists and is reported as not found.
AccountState.title: AccountState

Admission.description: The evidence that admits the registrant. Exactly one of an operator invite or a trust community's voucher.
Admission.title: Admission

didId.description: Fully-qualified DID identifier resolved from the most recent log entry (e.g. `did:webvh:<scid>:host:path`). Absent when `versionCount === 0`.

didUrl.description: Resolvable URL of the DID's log document (e.g. `https://did.example.com/alice/did.jsonl`). Stable across the record's lifetime: present from the initial reservation (`versionCount === 0`), it tells the owner where to publish the signed log and where resolvers fetch it. Distinct from `didId`, which only exists once a log entry has been published.

disabled.description: When `true`, the DID is administratively disabled — the host serves a deactivation marker but retains content for recovery within the host's retention policy.

domain.description: Hosting domain (hostname) under which the DID resolves. Matches the host segment of the embedded DID identifier.

method.description: DID method this record was registered under (e.g. `webvh`, `web`). When omitted, consumers MAY treat the record as legacy; SHOULD default to `webvh` only if their host predates the multi-method era.

mnemonic.description: Local path under which the DID is hosted (e.g. `alice`, `tenant/staff/alice`, `.well-known`). Compared by exact string equality (SPEC.md §4.8); producers SHOULD emit canonical form.

owner.description: VID of the party that currently owns the record. Authorization to mutate the record is anchored on this field.

totalResolves.description: Lifetime resolve counter, when the host exposes per-DID statistics.

updatedAt.description: RFC3339 timestamp of the most recent record mutation.

versionCount.description: Number of log entries the host currently holds for the DID. `0` indicates a reservation with no published log yet.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

HostingAccount.description: One account on a DID hosting service: who holds it, how it was admitted, and where it stands in the service's inactivity lifecycle.

admission.description: How the account was admitted: `invite`, an operator-issued invite; `voucher`, a voucher from a trust community the domain trusts. Absent for an account an administrator created directly.

disableAt.description: When the account's DIDs will be disabled if nothing keeps the account alive before then. Present for an `active` or `warned` account that is subject to expiry; absent for an account that is not (one an administrator exempted, for example) and for a `disabled` one.

domain.description: The hosting domain the account was admitted on. A self-registered account may hold DIDs on this domain only.

exempt.description: `true` when an administrator has exempted the account from its domain's terms (did-management/account/exempt): no path prefixes, agent names allowed, no inactivity lifecycle. Absent or `false`: the terms apply. Only on a self-registered account.

lastActiveAt.description: The last time the holder sent a task the service accepted, renewals included. A service MAY record this coarsely (for example at most once a day); it is a liveness signal, not an audit trail. Absent when the service has recorded none since registration.

lastResolvedAt.description: The last time any of the account's DIDs was resolved from the service, as far as the service knows. Absent when the service does not count resolutions toward liveness or has recorded none.

maxDidCount.description: The most DIDs the account may hold. Absent when the service does not state one.

maxTotalSizeBytes.description: The most bytes of DID content the account may hold in total. Absent when the service does not state one.

purgeAt.description: When a `disabled` account, its DIDs and its access are deleted. Present exactly when `state` is `disabled`.

role.description: The role the hosting service holds the account under, in the service's own role vocabulary (opaque here, as in the acl/* family) — for a self-registered account, its ordinary DID-owner role. What sets a self-registered account apart is not its role but its terms: its domain's path prefixes, quotas and inactivity lifecycle, and no agent names.

subject.description: The DID that holds the account, exactly as it authenticated when it registered. A `did:scid` subject is recorded without its `src` query parameter, which locates the log and is not part of the identity.

HostingAccount.title: HostingAccount

HostingVoucher.description: A trust community's signed statement that one DID may register an account with one hosting service. It is a credential: its own proof, by the community, for `assertionMethod`, carries the community's authority; the envelope proof of the register document carries only the registrant's.

@context.description: JSON-LD contexts, when the community issues the voucher as a JSON-LD credential. Absent: a plain JSON credential.

credentialSubject.description: Whom the voucher admits, and where.

domain.description: When present, the only hosting domain the voucher admits on.

hostingService.description: The DID of the hosting service the voucher is for: the register document's `recipient`. A voucher for one service is no use at another.

id.description: The DID the voucher admits, without any `src` query parameter. MUST be the identity the register document's `issuer` names.
The voucher's unique identifier. A consumer accepts each voucher once, keyed on (`issuer`, `id`), and keeps the record until `validUntil`.

issuer.description: The trust community's DID. The consumer accepts vouchers only from issuers the target domain lists as trusted.

proof.description: The community's W3C Data Integrity proof over the voucher. Closed, so that a member this schema does not name is refused rather than dropped: a proof that lost a signed member could not be verified.

@context.description: The voucher's own `@context`, which a JCS cryptosuite copies into the proof when the voucher carries one (eddsa-jcs-2022 §3.3.1). Absent otherwise.

created.description: When the community signed the voucher.

proofPurpose.description: Always `assertionMethod`: a voucher is an attestation.

verificationMethod.description: The community key that signed the voucher: a verification method of `issuer`, under its `assertionMethod` relationship.

type.description: Credential types. MUST include `DidHostingVoucher`; a validator does not check it.

validFrom.description: Before this instant the voucher is not yet valid. Absent: valid from issue.

validUntil.description: After this instant the voucher is no longer accepted. REQUIRED, so a consumer's single-use record is bounded.

HostingVoucher.title: HostingVoucher

invite.description: Both halves of an invite from did-management/account/invite/issue.

claimCode.description: The invite's claim code, delivered to the registrant separately from the token.

Referral.description: How a self-registered account came to the service, as attribution: who sent it (`via`) and a free-text note (`label`). Never authority — a service MUST NOT authorise anything on it.

label.description: A short note on the source — a campaign, an invitation's origin. Free text, never interpreted.

via.description: The DID of the party that sent the registrant, usually a trust community. Absent when only a `label` was given.

Referral.title: Referral

Response.description: The account the service created and the DID record it published. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.
Response.title: DID Management — Account Register — response payload

schema.description: A party with no account on a DID hosting service registers its own self-certifying DID there: it submits the DID's complete log and evidence that it is admitted (an operator invite or a trust community's voucher), and the service creates the account and publishes the DID in one commit. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

didData.description: The DID's complete log, from its genesis entry: for `webvh`, the `did.jsonl` content, one signed entry per line. At most 56 KiB, inside the document's 64 KiB: a self-registering DID's log is young.

domain.description: The hosting domain to register on. REQUIRED here, unlike in did-management/did/register: a party with no account has no default domain to fall back on, and the DID's identifier already names the host.

method.description: The DID method. This version admits `webvh` only, whose log is self-certifying: its SCID commits to the genesis entry, which names the DID and the keys that control it.

path.description: The path the DID is hosted under, `/`-separated (`g/agent-7f3a`): the DID's identifier names the same path with `:` separators (`did:webvh:{SCID}:{domain}:g:agent-7f3a`). It MUST be the path the identifier names, and MUST satisfy the domain's path rules as did-management/server/info publishes them.

referral.description: Optional: how the registrant came to the service, for attribution. Recorded on the account; never authority.

schema.title: DID Management — Account Register — payload
